title: Automotive Machining and Engine Repair
award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 16S/24Q to fewer than 30S/45Q units

program.section_heading: Certificate of Achievement-Advanced (COA-A) Automotive Machining and Engine Repair
outcomes: Demonstrate an application of four-stroke engine theory
Identify basic electrical circuits and diagnose automotive electrical circuit systems
Apply the basic principles of physics as they work in the automotive industry
Demonstrate knowledge of the job procurement process in the automotive industry
Demonstrate knowledge of estimates and repair orders
Demonstrate hazardous materials handling in the automotive industry

notes: The catalog prints this award as a Certificate of Achievement-Advanced (COA-A) of 44 units; De Anza uses quarter units, so 44 quarter units falls in the state's 24Q to fewer than 45Q category. Reviewer should confirm the COA-A is the award matching this state record.
Units are quarter units as printed by De Anza.
Catalog codes (e.g., AUTO 53A) correspond to closed-list codes with zero padding (AUTO 053A).
AUTO 53B is not in the closed list and is recorded as a catalog addition.
The section's description names 'an entry-level position in the automotive repair industry in engine diagnostics'; no specific job titles are listed, so careers left empty.

The section recommends one year of prior automotive experience (high school, ROP or De Anza's AUTO 50 series) and requires an Approved Automotive Technology Course Sequence Contract; these are not recorded as course blocks.

The final outcome in the COA-A section reads 'Demonstrate hazardous materials handling...' while the A.S. section reads 'Demonstrate knowledge of hazardous materials handling...'; the COA-A wording was copied as printed.
Text at the top of page 63 belongs to a different (automotive engine performance) program and was ignored; the A.S. section following the COA-A was not used.
